RUN.about: Cut by the lifecycle of one HTTP request — a caller configures ky, makes a request, then consumes the response — with retry logic and error handling branching from the request step.

issues.title: Without AbortSignal.any, only the last signal survives
issues.detail: When `AbortSignal.any` is unavailable, merging multiple signals via `.extend()` keeps only the last one. Earlier signals are silently discarded, so aborting them has no effect on the request.

children.title: Header Merging
children.sub: Headers are normalized to a lowercase plain object and merged with deletion support
children.detail: All header sources are converted to a plain object with lowercase keys via `toHeaderObject`. A value of `undefined` in a plain object, or the string `'undefined'` in a `Headers` instance, acts as a deletion marker.

rows.title: Apply deletions
rows.detail: An undefined value deletes the key. In a Headers instance, the string 'undefined' is treated as a deletion marker.

rows.title: Merge into result
rows.detail: Second source's entries overwrite the first's. Undefined values survive as deletion markers for later request construction.

issues.title: Header named __proto__ is silently dropped
issues.detail: When iterating entries in `toHeaderObject`, a header named `__proto__` is assigned via property access, which changes the prototype instead of creating an own property. The header is silently lost.

AUTHORED.title: Making a Request
AUTHORED.sub: Build the URL, set headers, serialize the body, run lifecycle hooks, and execute the fetch call with timeout and abort support.
AUTHORED.detail: The `Ky` class orchestrates a full request lifecycle: `Ky.create()` runs init hooks, builds a `Request`, enters `#run()` where hooks, fetch, and retry branching happen, then returns a `ResponsePromise` with body shortcuts.

children.title: Creating The Pipeline
children.sub: Ky.create() runs init hooks, instantiates Ky, and wraps the result in a ResponsePromise with body method shortcuts.
children.detail: `Ky.create()` is the only public entry. It runs synchronous `init` hooks on a cloned options object, constructs a `Ky` instance, then attaches `.json()`, `.text()`, `.bytes()` etc. shortcuts to the returned promise.

code.label: create() — init hooks, new Ky(), async result wrapper with try/finally cleanup
Body method shortcuts (.json(), .text(), etc.) attached to ResponsePromise
cloneInitHookOptions — deep-copies headers, json, searchParams, retry before init hooks

rows.title: Clone options for init hooks
rows.detail: Deep-copies headers, json, searchParams, retry, and context so init hook mutations don't leak across requests from the same instance.

rows.title: Run init hooks synchronously
rows.detail: Each init hook receives the mutable options object and can modify it in place. Errors here reject the promise but skip beforeError hooks.

rows.title: Construct Ky instance
rows.detail: Calls `new Ky(input, options)` which resolves the URL, serializes the body, merges headers, and builds the native Request.

rows.title: Attach body shortcuts
rows.detail: For each supported response type (json, text, formData, arrayBuffer, blob, bytes), adds a method that sets the Accept header and awaits the result with schema validation.

rows.title: Clean up on settle
rows.detail: A finally block cancels unused request bodies — the original and any retry clone — so streams are not leaked.

anatomy.caption: Body method shortcuts and their Accept headers

children.title: Building The Request
children.sub: The constructor resolves the URL, serializes JSON, merges headers, sets up abort signals, and creates a native Request.
children.detail: The constructor normalizes all options, resolves `prefix`/`baseUrl` with the input, JSON-stringifies `options.json`, manages the abort controller signal chain, and appends `searchParams` to the URL.

code.label: Constructor — full request building: validation, URL resolution, JSON body, headers, signal, searchParams
resolveInput() — joins prefix, resolves against baseUrl
applySearchParameters() — appends searchParams to the URL
#createManagedSignal — combines user signal with Ky's internal abort controller

rows.title: Validate input and options
rows.detail: Checks input type, rejects null for key options, validates context is an object, validates timeout and callback options.

rows.title: Normalize and merge
rows.detail: Merges headers from Request input and options, normalizes method to uppercase, normalizes retry options, applies defaults for throwHttpErrors/timeout/fetch.

rows.title: Resolve URL
rows.detail: `resolveInput()` joins string input with `prefix` (stripping trailing/leading slashes), then resolves against `baseUrl`. URL and Request inputs pass through.

rows.title: Serialize JSON body
rows.detail: If `options.json` is set, stringifies it (via custom `stringifyJson` or `JSON.stringify`) and sets content-type to application/json unless user provided one.

rows.title: Set up abort signal chain
rows.detail: Creates an internal AbortController and combines its signal with the user's signal via `AbortSignal.any()`. This managed signal is attached to the Request.

rows.title: Append search parameters
rows.detail: If `searchParams` has content, builds a new URL, applies deleted keys and new params, then recreates the Request with the updated URL.

anatomy.caption: How the URL is resolved from input, prefix, and baseUrl

issues.title: Inherited body lost when searchParams changes URL
issues.detail: When a Request input has a body and `searchParams` alter the URL, the Request is rebuilt. If the environment lacks request stream support or `keepalive`/`no-cors` is set, the inherited body is silently dropped.

children.title: Running Lifecycle Hooks
children.sub: Five hook types intercept the request at different stages: init, beforeRequest, afterResponse, beforeRetry, and beforeError.

group.note: Each hook type runs at a different stage; they are grouped by what they intercept.

children.detail: Hooks run inside `#run()` and `#retryFromError()`. Every async hook is raced against the `totalTimeout` budget, and can replace requests/responses, force retries, or transform errors.

code.label: #runBeforeRequestHooks — can return Request or Response
#runAfterResponseHooks — can replace Response or force retry
beforeRetry hooks inside #retryFromError — can stop, replace request, or return response
#throwProcessedError — runs beforeError hooks on every error
Hook type definitions: InitHook, BeforeRequestHook, BeforeRetryHook, BeforeErrorHook, AfterResponseHook

anatomy.caption: The five hook types and what each can do
Where each hook type intercepts the request lifecycle

issues.title: Hook-returned Response with failing status throws without retry
issues.detail: A Response returned from a `beforeRequest` or `beforeRetry` hook that has a non-2xx status is thrown as an HTTPError immediately, bypassing retry logic. The `#hookResponses` WeakSet marks these responses so the retry path is never entered.

children.title: Executing The Fetch
children.sub: Clones the request for retries, wraps upload progress, calls fetch with timeout, and maps raw errors to typed Ky errors.
children.detail: The `#fetch()` method clones the request when retries are enabled, wraps the body for upload progress, then calls fetch — either directly or through `timeout()`. Raw network errors become `NetworkError`.

code.label: #fetch() — clone, wrap upload progress, call fetch with timeout, map errors
#retry() — calls #fetch(), catches errors for retry
#getEffectiveTimeout — min of per-request timeout and remaining totalTimeout budget
#wrapRequestWithUploadProgress — streams request body for progress tracking

rows.title: Cancel previous attempt's body
rows.detail: Releases the unused upload body from any previous attempt via `cancelBody()`.

rows.title: Clone request for retries
rows.detail: If retry limit > 0, calls `request.clone()` and reattaches the managed signal. Skipped when retries disabled to avoid buffering large streams.

rows.title: Wrap upload progress
rows.detail: If `onUploadProgress` is configured and request streams are supported, pipes the body through a byte-counting TransformStream.

rows.title: Calculate effective timeout
rows.detail: Takes the minimum of per-request `timeout` and remaining `totalTimeout` budget. Returns `undefined` if neither applies.

rows.title: Call fetch or timeout(fetch)
rows.detail: Without timeout, calls `fetch(request)` directly. With timeout, calls `timeout()` which races fetch against a setTimeout.

rows.title: Map errors
rows.detail: Rethrows user aborts, wraps raw network errors into `NetworkError`, throws `TimeoutError` if totalTimeout exhausted.

anatomy.caption: Decision tree inside #fetch()

issues.title: Cloning streaming uploads buffers entire body in memory
issues.detail: When retries are enabled (the default), `request.clone()` calls `ReadableStream#tee()` which buffers the entire stream. For large uploads this causes excessive memory usage. Cloning is only skipped when retries are explicitly disabled.

children.title: Timeout Management
children.sub: Two timeout layers: per-request timeout races a single fetch, and totalTimeout caps the entire pipeline including retries.

group.note: Two independent timeout mechanisms that can both be active at once.

children.detail: The `timeout()` utility races a single fetch against a setTimeout (default 10s). The `totalTimeout` sets a wall-clock deadline at construction; `#raceWithTotalTimeout()` enforces it on every async operation.

code.label: timeout() — races fetch against setTimeout, aborts on expiry
#raceWithTotalTimeout — races any operation against remaining totalTimeout budget
Deadline set in constructor: performance.now() + totalTimeout
#getRemainingTotalTimeout — Math.max(0, deadline - now)
#getEffectiveTimeout — min(timeout, remaining totalTimeout)

rows.value: 10,000 ms (10 seconds)

rows.label: Per-request scope
rows.value: One fetch call — send to response headers

rows.label: totalTimeout default
rows.value: false (disabled)

rows.label: totalTimeout scope
rows.value: Entire pipeline: build + hooks + retries + body reads

rows.label: Clock source
rows.value: performance.now() ?? Date.now()

children.title: Upload And Download Progress
children.sub: Pipes request or response bodies through TransformStreams that count bytes and call progress callbacks.

group.note: Upload and download progress are independent features that share the same withProgress() helper.

children.detail: Both progress callbacks work by piping the body through a TransformStream that counts transferred bytes. Upload requires request stream support (`duplex: 'half'`); download adjusts for content-encoding.

code.label: withProgress() — TransformStream that counts bytes and calls the progress callback
streamResponse() — wraps response body for download progress, adjusts for content-encoding

issues.title: FormData size is an approximation that can overcount
issues.detail: The `getBodySize()` function estimates FormData size using a fixed boundary length constant that may differ from the runtime's actual boundary. The estimate errs high, so progress percent may reach its ceiling before the upload finishes.

children.title: Body Method Shortcuts
children.sub: Each shortcut sets an Accept header, awaits the response, and reads the body with timeout protection
children.detail: In `Ky.create`, a loop over `getSupportedResponseTypes()` attaches each body method to the result promise. `.json()` reads the body as text first, then parses; all others delegate directly to the native `Response` method, guarded by `#raceBodyRead`.

code.label: Loop attaching body shortcuts to the ResponsePromise
Non-json types: direct native call via #raceBodyRead
JSON path: text → parseJson → optional schema validation
#decorateResponse patches response.json with custom parseJson
responseTypes map: method name → Accept MIME type

anatomy.caption: What each shortcut does internally

rows.title: Set Accept header
rows.detail: If the request hasn't been sent yet, sets Accept to the MIME type matching the shortcut (e.g. `application/json` for `.json()`).

rows.title: Await the response
rows.detail: Waits for the inner fetch promise to resolve. If `ky.stop` was returned by a `beforeRetry` hook, the response is `undefined` and a TypeError is thrown.

rows.title: Read the body
rows.detail: Non-JSON shortcuts call the native method directly through `#raceBodyRead`. JSON reads `response.text()` first, then parses via `#parseJson` (custom or `JSON.parse`).

rows.title: Return or validate
rows.detail: If a schema was passed to `.json(schema)`, the parsed value is validated via `validateJsonWithSchema` before returning.

rows.label: Custom parseJson
rows.value: When `options.parseJson` is set, `#decorateResponse` also patches `response.json()` on the raw Response so both paths use it.

rows.label: .bytes() gating
rows.value: `getSupportedResponseTypes()` checks `Response.prototype.bytes` at runtime; the shortcut is omitted in environments that lack it.

rows.label: Empty body + schema
rows.value: When text is empty, a schema is passed, and no custom `parseJson` is set, the value is `undefined` instead of throwing a JSON parse error.

children.title: Schema Validation
children.sub: Validates parsed JSON against a Standard Schema V1 and throws SchemaValidationError on failure
children.detail: `validateJsonWithSchema` reads `schema['~standard'].validate`, awaits the result, and throws `SchemaValidationError` if `result.issues` is truthy. The error does not extend `KyError`, so `isKyError()` does not match it.

code.label: validateJsonWithSchema: validates and returns or throws
SchemaValidationError class with issues property
StandardSchemaV1 interface: the ~standard.validate contract
Issue, SuccessResult, FailureResult types

rows.title: Check schema shape
rows.detail: Reads `schema['~standard']` and verifies it is an object with a `validate` function. Throws `TypeError` if not.

rows.title: Call validate
rows.detail: Awaits `schema['~standard'].validate(jsonValue)`, which may be sync or async per the Standard Schema spec.

rows.title: Check issues
rows.detail: If `result.issues` is truthy, throws `new SchemaValidationError(result.issues)`. Otherwise returns `result.value`.

anatomy.caption: What SchemaValidationError looks like when caught

notes.label: Not a KyError
notes.value: Does not extend KyError — isKyError() returns false, so it won't be caught by KyError-specific handlers

notes.label: issues
notes.value: Readonly array of StandardSchemaV1Issue, each with message and optional path

rows.label: Supported validators
rows.value: Any library implementing Standard Schema V1: Zod 3.24+, Valibot, ArkType, etc.

rows.label: Called inside #raceWithTotalTimeout
rows.value: Validation runs within the totalTimeout budget; a slow validator can trigger a TimeoutError

children.title: Body Read Timeout
children.sub: Guards every body read against per-request timeout, totalTimeout, and user abort signals
children.detail: `#raceBodyRead` races the native body method against `timeout` and checks `totalTimeout` budget and user abort signals before and after. For `.json()`, parse and validation also run inside `#raceWithTotalTimeout`.

code.label: #raceBodyRead: races body read against timeout, checks abort
#getEffectiveTimeout: min of timeout and remaining totalTimeout
#raceWithTotalTimeout: totalTimeout budget guard for json parse
On timeout, aborts the controller since stream is locked

anatomy.caption: What can interrupt a body read

rows.label: Effective timeout
rows.value: min(options.timeout, remaining totalTimeout). If both are Infinity, no timeout is set.

rows.label: Network errors during read
rows.value: A raw TypeError from a dropped connection is wrapped in NetworkError and sent through beforeError hooks.

rows.label: Stream already locked
rows.value: On timeout, the body stream is locked by the reader, so #raceBodyRead aborts the controller instead of cancelling the stream.

rows.label: Abort wins over data
rows.value: Even if body bytes arrive before abort fires, a cancelled signal still rejects to prevent masking the cancellation.

children.title: Response Size Limiting
children.sub: Enforces maxResponseSize by wrapping the response body stream and throwing ResponseSizeError
children.detail: `limitResponseSize` wraps the body in a `TransformStream` counting bytes, throwing `ResponseSizeError` when `maxResponseSize` is exceeded. It patches native body methods because Chromium replaces stream errors with a generic TypeError.

code.label: limitResponseSize: wraps body stream with byte counter
copyResponseMetadata: patches body methods and preserves url/redirected/type
ResponseSizeError class with request and maxResponseSize
#limitResponseSize called on every response and hook replacement

rows.title: Check wrappable
rows.detail: `wrappableBody` returns undefined if the body is null, used, locked, or a null-body status (101, 103, 204, 205, 304). Size limiting is skipped.

rows.title: Pipe through counter
rows.detail: A TransformStream counts `transferredBytes += chunk.byteLength` and throws `ResponseSizeError` when the total exceeds `maxResponseSize`.

rows.title: Build new Response
rows.detail: A new `Response` is created with the wrapped body. `copyResponseMetadata` restores `url`, `redirected`, `type`, and `headers` from the original.

rows.title: Patch body methods
rows.detail: Each native body method is replaced with a wrapper that catches errors and re-throws the stored `ResponseSizeError` if one exists.

anatomy.caption: Null-body statuses that skip size limiting and progress

issues.title: Chromium replaces stream errors with generic TypeError
issues.detail: When a TransformStream throws inside `transform()`, Chromium's native body methods replace the error with a generic TypeError. The code works around this by patching every body method to re-throw the stored ResponseSizeError, but this relies on a WeakMap keyed by the body stream.

children.title: Download Progress
children.sub: Wraps the response body stream to report download progress via onDownloadProgress callback
children.detail: When `onDownloadProgress` is set, `#run` calls `streamResponse` which pipes the body through a `TransformStream` tracking bytes. Progress reports lag one chunk behind so `percent` never hits 100% early.

code.label: streamResponse: handles content-encoding and wires up progress
withProgress: TransformStream that tracks bytes and calls back
#run wraps response with streamResponse when onDownloadProgress is set
wrappableBody: guards against locked, used, or null-body responses

rows.title: Determine total bytes
rows.detail: Uses `content-length` unless `content-encoding` is set (compressed responses make the header inaccurate). Unknown total is `0`.

rows.title: Pipe through withProgress
rows.detail: A TransformStream enqueues each chunk, then reports the *previous* chunk's byte count. This one-chunk delay prevents `percent` from reaching 100% early.

rows.title: Cap percent below 100%
rows.detail: While streaming, `percent` is capped at `1 - Number.EPSILON`. If `totalBytes` is inaccurate, `reportedTotalBytes` adjusts upward.

rows.title: Final flush
rows.detail: The `flush` callback fires with `percent: 1` and `totalBytes` set to the actual `transferredBytes`, guaranteeing an accurate final event.

anatomy.caption: Shape of each progress callback argument

notes.label: percent
notes.value: 0 to 1 - Number.EPSILON during streaming, exactly 1 on the final flush event

notes.label: totalBytes
notes.value: From content-length when uncompressed, 0 when unknown, true transferred bytes on final event

rows.label: Requires ReadableStream
rows.value: If the environment lacks ReadableStream, an Error is thrown before wrapping: 'Streams are not supported in your environment'.

rows.label: Compressed responses
rows.value: content-encoding other than 'identity' makes totalBytes 0, since content-length counts wire bytes but progress counts decompressed bytes.

children.title: Backoff and Jitter
children.sub: Exponential delay with optional jitter and a configurable cap

Default delay formula

rows.title: Call retry.delay(attempt)
rows.detail: Default: 0.3 * 2^(attempt-1) * 1000. Must return a non-negative number or Infinity; anything else throws TypeError with the original error as cause.

rows.title: Apply jitter
rows.detail: If jitter is true: Math.random() * delay (full jitter). If jitter is a function: jitter(delay). Invalid function result silently falls back to un-jittered delay.

rows.title: Cap with backoffLimit
rows.detail: Return Math.min(backoffLimit, jitteredDelay). Default backoffLimit is Infinity. Final result is also capped at maxSafeTimeout (2^31 - 1 ms) before reaching setTimeout.

rows.label: Full jitter purpose
rows.value: Prevents thundering herd when many clients retry simultaneously after a shared failure

rows.label: Server timing exemption
rows.value: Jitter is never applied to server-provided Retry-After delays, only to calculated backoff

rows.label: maxSafeTimeout
rows.value: 2,147,483,647 ms (~25 days): the maximum 32-bit int, preventing setTimeout overflow

children.title: Executing the Retry
children.sub: The retry loop that waits, runs hooks, and re-fetches
children.detail: `#retryFromError` checks the totalTimeout budget, waits for the delay, resets the abort controller if the previous attempt timed out, applies any custom request from ForceRetryError, then runs `beforeRetry` hooks before re-fetching.

rows.title: Check totalTimeout budget
rows.detail: If remaining budget is 0, throw TimeoutError. If the delay alone would consume all remaining budget, wait it out then throw.

rows.title: Wait for delay
rows.detail: await delay(retryDelay, {signal: userAbortSignal}). Only the user's abort signal can interrupt the wait, not Ky's internal controller.

rows.title: Reset abort controller
rows.detail: If the previous attempt was aborted (e.g. per-request timeout), create a fresh AbortController and managed signal for the retry.

rows.title: Apply custom request
rows.detail: For ForceRetryError with a custom Request, replace the current request. The custom request's signal is swapped for Ky's managed signal.

rows.title: Run beforeRetry hooks
rows.detail: Each hook receives {request, options, error, retryCount}. A hook can return a Request, Response, ky.stop, or {options} to modify settings.

rows.title: Increment and re-fetch
rows.detail: Increment retryCount and call #retry(), which calls #fetch(). On failure, the whole loop repeats from the decision step.
